author: reek
body: FactDisk is how the compiler reads a work out of the fact store: the quotation gate reaches it from `opening.codex`, and until this test nothing had ever run a line of it. The two fact-log disks that existed (`disk-facts-read.disk`, `disk-facts-load.disk`) hold a single kind-0 entry each, so the source-definition decode path -- the entire reason the chapter exists -- had no fixture at all.

author: reek
body: The disk here is minted by `build/mint-factlog-fixture.ps1` from the SPECIFICATION: Foreword chapter FactLog for the sector layout, Foreword chapter SourceDefWire for the record format. It is deliberately NOT produced by running DiskFacts. A fixture written by the writer under test proves only that the reader agrees with its own writer, which is the failure `BrotliBeatsOpus` is about, and the reason the reverse direction gets written first.

author: reek
body: Three entries, in an order chosen to be adversarial:

author: reek
body: The kind-0 entry is FIRST on purpose. A walk that stopped at the first entry it could not decode would report zero works, and a walk that decoded it anyway would report three.

author: reek
body: The signed and unsigned records are both present because `fd-admit-work` routes them differently: an empty signature is OFFERED and a real one is PUBLISHED, and only the published one belongs in the bundle's signed map. A reader that published everything would look identical on a count.

author: reek
body: The last two lines are the supplement property. The compiler hands `store-read-bundle` the bundle it already built from the offered-works blob, so the disk must ADD to it and not replace it: a quotation the blob already satisfied has to still resolve afterwards.
